verses.1: And do not ignore this, brothers. For I say that the law requires that man be bound by it for as long as he lives.
verses.2: For a woman who is married to a man, she is subject to the laws of that man. But if the man dies, then she is no longer subject to those laws.
verses.3: Therefore, if a man becomes the husband of another woman through adultery, then that woman is no longer considered a married woman under the law. But if the man dies, then she becomes free from the law, as she no longer has any legal status as a married woman.
verses.4: So, brothers, you also died according to the law, through the body of Christ. This was so that you might be raised from the dead and become participants in God’s kingdom.
verses.5: For when we were still in this flesh, the sufferings caused by our sins were carried out within us, leading to our death.
verses.6: Now, we are no longer bound by that law; we have died within its framework. Thus, we can serve in a way that is consistent with the spirit of the times, rather than being confined by the old rules of writing.
verses.7: So, what should we do? Is the law a sin? It doesn’t happen that way. Instead, one cannot recognize sin unless it is mentioned by the law. After all, one cannot understand lust unless the law says so. You won’t desire anything.
verses.8: And taking advantage of this commandment, sin brought about all kinds of desires in me. For according to the law, sin is a death sentence.
verses.9: But I never acted against the law. When the command was given, my sin still persisted.
verses.10: I, however, died. And I found that command: to live meant to die.
verses.11: For the sin, having taken hold of me through that commandment, it drove me away and also caused me to be destroyed by it.
verses.12: So, the law is holy, and the commands are also holy, just, and good.
verses.13: So, was it a good death for me? No. It was rather a sin that caused death through the action of this “good” deed. In other words, it was a sin that became excessive due to the command given by God.
verses.14: We know that the law is spiritual. I, however, am a fleshly being, subject to sin.
verses.15: For what I do, I don’t know why I do it. I don’t do it because I want to, but rather because I hate doing it.
verses.16: But if I do not want to do this, then it is in accordance with the law that it is right to do so.
verses.17: Now, I no longer work on it anymore; rather, the sin that lies within me is what causes this problem.
verses.18: I know that it doesn’t reside within me. It’s in my flesh. It’s good to want something for me, but it’s not good to actually work towards achieving that thing.
verses.19: For I do not do what is good, but rather what I do not want to do.
verses.20: But if I don’t want to do this, then I will no longer do it. It’s the sin of having a wife in my life that makes me do this.
verses.21: I find therefore that the law serves the purpose of doing what is good for me, while preventing me from doing what is bad.
verses.22: For I am eager for the law of God to be fulfilled in human beings.
verses.23: I see, however, that there is another law among my followers that contradicts my own law. This law makes me feel weak and helpless in the face of the evil that exists among my followers.
verses.24: I’m a poor man. Who will remove me from the body of death?
verses.25: For the sake of God, through Jesus Christ, our Lord. Therefore, I serve the law of God with my mind, but with my body I follow the law of sin.
